subject: Workload snapshot & ops asks — post-demo follow-up
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samuel Wong <samuel.wong@atlashealth.ai>, Priya Desai <priya@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Workload snapshot & ops asks — post-demo follow-up

Hi Samuel / Priya,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for walking us through AtlasHealth's inference use cases. As promised, a short recap and the three asks we need to finalize a sizing recommendation for Dedicated / Private deployment:

1) Steady vs peak profile (tokens/QPS): please confirm the typical 24-hr steady state and the expected peak windows (duration + multiplicative factor). From our call I captured: steady ~250 QPS (short text requests), 1.8k tokens/sec average across requests; daily peak ~4x for ~20 minutes. Can you confirm?

2) Concurrency & streaming: do you expect streaming responses for the majority of calls (yes/no)? If streaming, what's the % of requests that require server-sent partial tokens vs fully-batched complete responses? Any strict tail-latency SLO for first-byte ?

3) Long context / KV cache needs: do you use >8k token contexts for any workflows (diagnostic notes ingestion, long-policy summarization)? If so, what % of requests hit >8k vs <2k.

Next steps: if you can drop a small sample CSV with per-request token counts / start times (anonymized) we'll run a quick throughput simulation and return a recommended GPU pool + concurrency profile and an SLO risk matrix. The sample doesn't need payloads — just timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, and whether streaming.

I've CC'd Marcus from our infra team who will review the sample and SLO matrix once we return it.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Workload snapshot & ops asks — post-demo follow-up

Thanks Neha — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Steady/Peak: steady is closer to 180–220 QPS (median 200), but your call had a slightly higher estimate because of bursty batch jobs. Peak is usually caused by our nightly clinician-assist jobs and a few morning spikes — peaks are ~5x steady and typically last 10–25 minutes.

- Tokens: per-request tokens vary a lot. Most patient-summary requests are 300–700 tokens in/out. The clinician-assist batch jobs are the heavy tail: 4–12k tokens per request but only ~0.2% of total requests.

- Streaming: about 35% of interactive sessions use streaming (progressive transcript), the rest are synchronous responses. For streaming we care about first-token latency <120ms 95th. For synchronous we want 95th <350ms.

- Long contexts: yes — the batch jobs and a small set of analytic pipelines use contexts >8k. That's rare but important.

We'll drop an anonymized CSV with the last 72hrs of request metadata by EOD (Priya will attach).

Samuel
VP Product
AtlasHealth
samuel.wong@atlashealth.ai

- Run a quick throughput simulation against two baseline model profiles (Llama2-70B-q4 -> quantized variant, and an LLM-CHAT-16k) to estimate tokens/sec and GPU concurrency needs.
- Produce an SLO risk table showing latency risk at different concurrency/batching knobs and an ops playbook for graceful fallback to smaller models during peaks.
- Recommend Dedicated pool sizing (min/max GPU count), preferred instance families, and a suggested KV cache strategy for the >8k flows.

Attached: a blank slo_matrix.xlsx and a tiny sample (workload_sample.csv) template to copy. If you can send the real CSV, we'll aim to return an initial sizing + SLO matrix in 48 hours.

Subject: Internal: AtlasHealth sample incoming — quick triage notes

Neha — thanks for the ping. Once the CSV arrives let's do the following internal checklist before we hand off to perf sims: 

- Sanity check: validate timestamps are monotonic and time zone normalized; detect any clear outliers (>99.9th token counts) and flag as batch-only.
- Token distribution: split into percentiles (10/50/90/99) for tokens_in and tokens_out — this will inform batching knobs and KV cache sizing.
- Streaming fraction: compute percent streaming per hour to see if streaming windows align with peaks.
- SLO targets: align on two SLO profiles (interactive: 95th first-byte <120ms; transactional: 95th end-to-end <350ms).

Rishi and I will run a quick internal sim (local cluster) and aim to have a draft SLO impact table back to Neha in 36–48 hours after receipt. I'll create a short report and attach a recommended Dedicated pool config (min GPUs, burst headroom).

Marcus Lin
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
